purpose: Connectivity sensitivity only. No water levels, discharge or inundation predictions.
crossingRoutePolicy: Straight chord between mapped western trace endpoint and eastern channel start. Approximate search corridor, not a surveyed culvert alignment.

roadContext.name: Manor Road
roadContext.status: Bounded 1900 carriageway restored in 3D, with a profile from three 1890s road spot heights. Railway alignment locally retraced; railway formation height remains provisional.

scenarios.name: Mapped channel only
scenarios.description: Only the identifiable eastern channel is connected. Unknown links are excluded, which does not establish that they were historically blocked.

scenarios.name: Crossing blocked
scenarios.description: Assume the western feature is a drain and its sluices pass water, but the railway/road crossing is blocked.

scenarios.name: East to west — working model
scenarios.description: Preferred reconstruction: culverted drainage passes water east to west when western water levels permit, with controls preventing return flow. Nearby ground levels and mapped sluices support this interpretation; pipe dimensions and gate mechanism remain provisional. Arrows indicate intended passage, not continuous flow.

scenarios.name: One-way: west to east
scenarios.description: Assume the opposite gate orientation, with western sluices passing water. Direction is a scenario, not historical evidence.

scenarios.name: Unrestricted connection
scenarios.description: Assume an open crossing in both directions and passing western sluices. This is an upper bound on possible connections, not on flood extent or flow capacity.

evidenceReview.source: West Ham: a study in social and industrial problems (1907), printed p29 note1, PDF p53
evidenceReview.finding: Describes replacement of marsh watercourses by building sites and shortcomings in sewer capacity and pumping exposed by the 1888 flood.
evidenceReview.modelUse: Do not assume surviving mapped drains provide a free gravity outfall. Does not supply the local culvert dimensions or invert.

evidenceReview.source: Jim Clifford, West Ham and the River Lea, chapter6, PDF p182 and note21
evidenceReview.file: West Ham and the River Lea_ A Social and E - Jim Clifford.pdf
evidenceReview.finding: Reports pump stoppage when flooding extinguished the fires in 1875 and 1888; the 1888 pump house required a fire engine to drain it.
evidenceReview.modelUse: Future flood scenarios must consider pumping failure separately from channel connectivity; no pump link or capacity assigned here.

evidenceReview.finding: Railway and Marsh Lane are visible, but internal field drainage is sparsely represented.
evidenceReview.modelUse: No nineteenth-century drain disappearance or construction date inferred from omission. Do not copy the 1900 graph into 1850.

evidenceReview.finding: A Manor Road drainage agreement is with Hackney Borough Council, dated18June1906.
evidenceReview.modelUse: Rejected as confirmation of this West Ham crossing; same road name is insufficient.

workingInterpretation.status: preferred engineering inference, not surveyed pipe detail
workingInterpretation.connection: Ditches on opposite sides of the embankment, their alignment and mapped sluices support a probable culverted drainage connection. Treating them as disconnected is a sensitivity case, not the preferred reconstruction.

levelEvidence.interpretation: Ground beside this reach is approximately 0.4–0.6 m higher to the east. This supports the preferred direction but does not measure invert slope or water-level difference.

workingInterpretation.gateInterpretation: The one-way scenario approximates successful controlled drainage. A sluice label alone does not establish a flap gate, automatic operation, or constant east-to-west flow. High downstream water can stop drainage; ineffective or open controls may allow return flow.
